 Melina Khan USA TODAY Nov. 2, 2026, 8:03 a.m. ET Hear this story Some toddler snack bars have been recalled for a potentially fatal choking hazard after several consumer complaints, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration .
 On Oct. 30, Once Upon a Farm issued a recall of all flavors of its Tractor Wheels soft-baked bars, which were sold at retailers including Walmart, Target and Costco, according to an FDA notice .
 The FDA said it received several reports of toddlers between 1.5-2.5 years old whose airways were completely obstructed and were unable to breathe after consuming the product.
 "We know that parents place their trust in us every time they buy one of our products. We fell short of that, and that is why we are taking these aggressive actions," Once Upon a Farm said in a statement .
 Here's what to know.

 All Once Upon a Farm Tractor Wheels organic toddler soft-baked bars have been recalled.
 The recall applies to all flavors, including the following:
 Apple, Sweet Potato, & Spinach Tractor Wheels  
 Strawberry, Pumpkin, & Beet Tractor Wheels 
 Banana, Pumpkin & Cauliflower Tractor Wheels 
 Why were Once Upon a Farm snack bars recalled?
 The snack bars were recalled after the FDA received multiple consumer reports about toddlers who choked on them.
 According to the FDA, when the bars are chewed, they reportedly form a dry, sticky mass that may not be dislodged using standard choking interventions like back blows and the Heimlich maneuver.
 The FDA said some choking incidents have required emergency response intervention and hospital observation.
 Where were recalled snack bars sold?
 The products were sold nationwide, including at Costco, Target and Walmart stores as well as online retailers, according to the FDA.

 What to do if you have recalled Once Upon a Farm snack bars
 Anyone who has the recalled snack bars should throw them away.
 Consumers can return the product to location of purchase for a full refund or contact care@uponafarm.com .
